pairs.difference: A: the pumpkin bucket is even moulded plastic with a soft sheen, the candies are glossier, and the table has fine quiet grain, so the card holds two gloss levels. B: the beach ball panels are almost textureless, with a blown white glow on the upper-right panel and muddy pink bleeding into the white panels. Gloss and detail are below the real range. Only coarse specks on the sand carry any texture.
pairs.fix: Draw the beach ball as thin vinyl with one small crisp highlight and narrow welded seams between panels. Keep the white panels clean, with no pink haze.

pairs.difference: A: every scroll of the gate is the same lacquered copper with a hard rim light, and the bricks and paving are crisply edged. Detail, micro-texture and gloss all sit above the real range. Wrought iron reads as glazed toy plastic. B: the spyglass has a quiet fine wrinkle in the dark leather, satin brass and a glossy lens, so the materials are separated and the marks are small.
pairs.fix: Paint the gate as dull dark wrought iron with soft matte shading and only a few small highlights. Soften the brick edges and remove the bright outline along every scroll.

pairs.difference: A: the castle stone is soft and matte with quiet block joints, and the door wood has simple plank lines, which is close to the real restraint. B: the door has wavy streaks in its blue paint, crisp hard-edged ivy and chunky clay-like flowers across the whole frame. Micro-texture and gloss are well above the real range, so the card is busy with sharp marks everywhere.
pairs.fix: Paint the door as smooth satin blue with no streaks. Reduce the ivy to fewer soft leaves and let the flowers melt softly into the shading, with no sharp outlines.

pairs.difference: A: the bark on the tree is big flowing grain, decorative but smoothly shaded and matte with low noise. B: the topiary is hundreds of near-identical crisp leaves, each with a bright glossy edge. Micro-texture and gloss are above the real range, so foliage reads as repeated shiny plastic stamps rather than a soft mass.
pairs.fix: Paint the bush as a soft leafy mass with only a few defined leaves near the top light. Keep the rest matte and blurred together, with no bright rim on each leaf.

pairs.difference: A: the chest wood carries large dark-lined grain, a decorative knot and scratch marks, and its gritty rivets sit next to a lacquered padlock. Texture scale is big and detail just passes the real ceiling. B: the ice tray has a satin rubbery tray and glassy cubes, though the frost speckle along its edges is a noisy sprinkle.
pairs.fix: Make the wood grain thin and faint, with no knots or scratches. Keep the iron bands flat matte grey and leave the padlock as the only shiny part.

pairs.difference: A: the bag has an all-over crisp canvas weave and dashed stitching around the patch, plus lacquered handles beside it, a fine textile detail that the real cards tend to leave out. B: the seahorse is soft airbrushed skin with a faint matte grain and a single glossy eye, smooth and low in detail like the real restraint.
pairs.fix: Remove the visible weave and show the fabric as a soft smooth matte surface. Keep only a few subtle stitches around the patch.

pairs.difference: A: the bracelet is smooth soft silicone with low gloss and slightly blurred highlights. B: the bat is soft airbrushed matte with a gentle sheen on the belly and wings. Both sit in the real range, and neither shows surface noise or oversized detail.

A: the bottle is soft translucent frosted plastic with a blurred highlight, a very quiet surface and a low-detail reading like the real cards, though at the bottom of the detail range. B: the flask has a crisp bright rim line, iridescent soap-bubble spheres and sharp window reflections, so the glass is more polished than the real restraint.
pairs.fix: Draw the glass with one soft window highlight and a thin faint rim. Make the bubbles plain pale green with no rainbow sheen.

pairs.difference: A: the car has a hard lacquered body with bright streaks along every curve, gold trim with sharp rim light, and crisp spokes and headlight rings. Detail, micro-texture and gloss are far above the real range, and glass, paint and trim share one varnished finish. B: the boat has quiet matte wood planks with soft lines and softly twisted rope, all within the real range.
pairs.fix: Paint the car body as soft satin dark paint with one broad highlight on the roof. Dull the gold trim, reduce the spokes to simple soft shapes and remove the white streaks along the curves.

pairs.difference: A: the whistle is very smooth matte-satin plastic with a soft gradient and blurred edges, under-detailed but physically plausible. B: the web is one uniform pearly tube material with a sharpened light halo along each strand and beaded joints, so silk reads as moulded plastic, and highlight share is above the real range.
pairs.fix: Draw the web as thin soft pale threads without tube shading. Remove the balls at the joints and the bright outline along each strand.

pairs.difference: A: the skull is one uniform matte clay with no pores, cracks or sheen on the teeth, and its gloss, detail and micro-texture fall below the real range. B: the sneakers separate rubber sole, mesh dots and shiny laces, which gives a mixed gloss range, though the mesh and laces are busy and at the top of the real range.
pairs.fix: Give the skull a dry bone surface with faint fine pits, a slightly shinier enamel on the teeth and a glossy finish on the orange paint marks.

pairs.difference: A: the teal cover is plain smooth board with crisp sticker edges and a loud streaky wood table behind. B: the purple cover has an all-over pebbled leather grain, a dashed stitch line and bright satin gold fittings, matching the added stitches and grain seen on generated lesson cards. The numbers lean slightly the other way, with A just over the real ceiling, so this is a low-confidence call.
pairs.fix: Show the cover as smooth soft leather without pebbling and drop the dashed stitch line. Keep the gold corners matte, with one small highlight on the gem.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away mostly through surfaces that are too finished. The same lacquered finish and hard rim light run across all materials, and crisp fine detail is spread evenly over the card: repeated leaves, scrollwork, canvas weave, pebbled leather and dashed stitches. Real cards stay soft and quiet, leave most surfaces plain, and keep gloss to one or two places. A second, weaker tell is the opposite extreme: a single featureless clay or vinyl surface with no gloss variation.
